title: Brief special meeting to authorize closed session
subtitle: Start time moved earlier; labour relations matter referred to in-camera discussion; no delegations or mayoral updates.
overview: Council held a short special meeting on September 25, 2023, that began at 4:59 p.m. rather than the scheduled 5:30 p.m. Council first agreed to waive notice so the meeting could start immediately {{vote:m1}}. Changing the start time required two-thirds of the whole of Council.

The only other business was authorizing a closed session. Council voted to hold an in-camera meeting right after the special meeting to consider a labour relations matter, as permitted by the Municipal Act, 2001 {{vote:m2}}.

No pecuniary interests were declared, no delegations appeared and the Mayor had no updates. The meeting adjourned at 5:03 p.m. For residents, the meeting made no policy or spending decisions. It only set up a private discussion, and the minutes report no outcome from that closed session.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a closed meeting immediately after the special meeting to consider a labour relations matter under Section 239 (d) of the Municipal Act, 2001 {{vote:m2}}.

decisions.item: Waive notice to change start time
decisions.detail: Council waived notice so the special meeting could begin immediately instead of at 5:30 p.m. {{vote:m1}}.

debate: There was no substantive debate; each motion was moved, seconded and put to a vote.
The chair explained the meeting was starting early only so the closed session could be authorized.
No delegations were registered, and no written comments were noted in the minutes.
